key_insight: GenWildSplat is a feed-forward 3D reconstruction framework that generalizes across outdoor scenes and reliably reconstructs geometry from sparse, unposed images despite varying illumination and transient occlusions—without costly per‑scene optimization or scene‑specific appearance embeddings.
problem_solved: Reconstructing accurate 3D geometry from a small number of unposed, real‑world images is brittle: existing methods rely on per‑scene optimization or appearance embeddings, fail under sparse views and changing lighting/occluders, and do not generalize across diverse outdoor scenes.
method: Feed‑forward network trained on diverse outdoor data to predict geometry from sparse, unposed image sets (no per‑scene optimization).
Aggregation of multi‑view features with modules that promote geometric consistency and suppress transient appearance (illumination changes, moving occluders).
Design and evaluation choices that prioritize generalization: training across scenes and measuring performance on held‑out, realistic outdoor datasets.
impact: Enables fast, generalizable sparse‑view 3D reconstruction for real‑world applications (mapping, AR/VR, robotics) by removing heavy per‑scene tuning and improving robustness to lighting and transient occlusions, making large‑scale deployment more practical.
visual_elements: Before/after panel: sparse input photos (2–6 views) vs predicted depth/mesh renderings to show reconstruction quality.
Pipeline diagram: feed‑forward architecture showing multi‑view feature aggregation, transient suppression, and geometry output (depth/mesh).
Robustness chart: reconstruction accuracy vs number of input views, with curves for GenWildSplat and prior methods, plus examples under varying illumination/occlusion.
Qualitative montage: diverse outdoor scenes (different lighting, moving objects) with predicted geometry overlays to illustrate generalization.
paper_title: Generalizable Sparse-View 3D Reconstruction from Unconstrained Images
paper_authors: Vinayak Gupta, Chih-Hao Lin, Shenlong Wang, Anand Bhattad, Jia-Bin Huang
